correctness.rationale: The already-published bipartite and unique-largest-part cases reduce the proof to at least three parts with the maximum part size attained twice. For odd order, a Hamiltonian cyclic ordering of part labels and the sum coloring on \(\mathbb Z_N\) make every missing-color set a translate of a part with no adjacent residues. For even order, the one-factorization on \(\mathbb Z_{N-1}\cup\{\infty\}\), the specially spaced smallest part and a step-two Hamilton cycle force every same-part omission to avoid consecutive colors. Dirac's theorem supplies the required cyclic words. I independently stress-tested the construction on all tied-maximum multipartite profiles through order 12 with no violation; the packaged verifier extends the same finite stress test through order 16.
risks: The proof uses Casselgren--Petrosyan's published unique-largest-part theorem as an input.
The exact interval-colorability subclass remains a separate problem.
